newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds poised for sovereign issue-fest.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds poised for sovereign issue-fest.

text.p: The primary market was bracing itself for a flood of sovereign issues on Thursday, syndicate managers said.

Russia was due to launch its long-awaited third Eurobond, a 10-year deal it said would total at least $1.0 billion but which bankers said had easily enough demand for a deal worth $1.5 billion and possibly even $2.0 billion.
A launch spread around 375 basis points was widely forecast.
China was due launch a 500 million mark five-year Eurobond at 55-60 b.p. over Bunds.

At an investor presentation in London this week, China said it wanted to establish itself with European investors ahead of the European Union's planned single currency. Investor focus is also on the handover of Hong Kong to China -- now 12 days away.

It will be the first transaction for China this year, and the first since it was upgraded by Standard and Poor's in May. The upcoming deal is also China's second mark Eurobond after a 10-year absence from the market. China is rated A3 by Moody's Investors Service and BBB+ by S&P.
Credit Suisse First Boston and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell are joint lead managers.
Mexico's proposed $1.0 billion five-year global FRN was expected to be launched and priced around 140 b.p. over three-month LIBOR, syndicate sources said.
The deal will likely be callable in June 2000.
HSBC and Merrill Lynch are joint lead managers.
On Tuesday, Mexico said it would call an outstanding $6.0 billion FRN secured by Pemex oil receivables which it issued last August.
The FRN will go towards that deal's refinancing.
Cyprus will make its Euromarket debut with a $200-$300 million five-year deal.
Ioannis Ioannou, head of the external debt section at the Central Bank of Cyprus, said earlier this week the deal would be priced at a spread in the mid-30s b.p.
The transaction will be lead managed by SBC Warburg and issued under Cyprus' recently established $500 million EMTN programme.
Ioannou said it was unlikely Cyprus would launch any further international bonds this year.
